task/landing-page347962dSupport project-relative language paths across repositories
  • UI
    Chat send

    The composer hands the text to the chats actions

  • State
    POST /api/chats/{id}/messages

    Fetch adapter — no credential is attached to the request

  • UI
    Failed-turn chip
    1. Only chat.latestTurn can show an error, so the login hint disappears from the timeline as soon as the next turn starts — even if that one is still running.
    2. The chip splits the message at the first blank line (line 26): the hint's first sentence shows inline and the remediation collapses behind Details, which is why the constant in claude-stream.ts:53 is written as blank-line-separated paragraphs.
    3. It renders with whitespace-pre-wrap and no markdown, so the hint's numbered steps survive as literal text.
  • Route
    send endpoint

    Starts a turn; the reply is just the chat with a placeholder

  • Route
    chat WebSocket

    turn-completed carries the auth failure back, not the POST

  • Service
    ChatsService.send

    Nothing on the request path checks or supplies credentials — the service only decides between starting and queueing, so an unauthenticated chat still costs a full process spawn and returns HTTP 200 before failing asynchronously.

  • Service
    spawn the agent CLI
    1. The child inherits process.env verbatim, so the credential reaches the CLI only if it was already in the server's environment or is set by the login shell — reviewer adds nothing auth-related.
    2. The only variables reviewer injects are MAX_THINKING_TOKENS (providers.ts:189) plus REVIEWER_CHAT_ID and REVIEWER_API.
    3. The prompt goes over stdin rather than argv, so nothing sensitive in a message lands in the process table.
  • Process
    $SHELL -l -c
    1. Turns run through a login, non-interactive shell (-l -c), so ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc are never sourced — the credential export has to be in ~/.zshenv/~/.zprofile or ~/.bash_profile.
    2. Every turn is a fresh shell, so a newly exported token is picked up without restarting the server — and equally, a token exported only in the server's own terminal session dies with it.
    3. The command -v guard means a missing CLI exits 127 with a plain message rather than looking like an auth failure.

    Model discovery runs its CLI probes through a login plus interactive shell (-l -i -c) while chat turns use -l -c, so a token exported from ~/.zshrc populates the model picker while every turn on that provider fails to authenticate.

  • Service
    result line → auth failure
    1. Auth failure is detected by matching a regex against the CLI's own reply text (claude-stream.ts:39), not by an exit code or an error field — a result line with is_error: false still settles as a failed turn.
    2. The login prompt is only scrubbed from the streamed reply when the buffer is under 200 characters (line 341), so a longer logged-out answer would be shown as the assistant's message and flagged as an error.
    3. Each provider owns its own pattern and hint: cursor's live in cursor-stream.ts:44 and 53, and codex/opencode have none at all.
  • Service
    finalizeTurn / loginHint
    1. This is the second detection site, for the case the parsers can't see: a CLI that dies with the login prompt on stderr and never emits a result line.
    2. It only inspects the last 500 characters of stderr (line 377), so a login prompt printed early in a noisy failure is missed and the raw tail is shown instead.
    3. loginHint returns null for codex and opencode (turn-parser.ts:81), so those two providers surface their raw CLI error with no remediation text.
  • Store
    completeTurn → chats.json

    The hint is written into chats.json as the turn's errorMessage, so a chat reopened after the developer has logged back in still shows the stale login advice on that old turn.

  • External
    The developer's own CLI login
    1. reviewer holds no LLM credential at all — there is no key field, no keychain entry, and no settings screen; the only occurrences of CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in the repo are inside the hint text on lines 72 and 81 of this file.
    2. Auth is therefore whatever the CLI already has on this machine: an interactive /login token, or a long-lived one from claude setup-token exported into the environment.
    3. Because the credential lives one process away, the server can only ever recognise a failure after the fact — it cannot pre-check whether a turn will authenticate.
    1. The remediation the hint suggests happens on a different rail: terminal threads launch the same CLIs through $SHELL -l -i inside a PTY, which is the only place an interactive /login can actually run.
    2. That PTY path is login and interactive, so it sources ~/.zshrc — which is exactly why a token exported there works when you type claude in a reviewer terminal but not in a chat turn.

task/landing-page347962dSupport project-relative language paths across repositories
  • UI
    Chat send

    The composer hands the text to the chats actions

  • State
    POST /api/chats/{id}/messages

    Fetch adapter — no credential is attached to the request

  • UI
    Failed-turn chip
    1. Only chat.latestTurn can show an error, so the login hint disappears from the timeline as soon as the next turn starts — even if that one is still running.
    2. The chip splits the message at the first blank line (line 26): the hint's first sentence shows inline and the remediation collapses behind Details, which is why the constant in claude-stream.ts:53 is written as blank-line-separated paragraphs.
    3. It renders with whitespace-pre-wrap and no markdown, so the hint's numbered steps survive as literal text.
  • Route
    send endpoint

    Starts a turn; the reply is just the chat with a placeholder

  • Route
    chat WebSocket

    turn-completed carries the auth failure back, not the POST

  • Service
    ChatsService.send

    Nothing on the request path checks or supplies credentials — the service only decides between starting and queueing, so an unauthenticated chat still costs a full process spawn and returns HTTP 200 before failing asynchronously.

  • Service
    spawn the agent CLI
    1. The child inherits process.env verbatim, so the credential reaches the CLI only if it was already in the server's environment or is set by the login shell — reviewer adds nothing auth-related.
    2. The only variables reviewer injects are MAX_THINKING_TOKENS (providers.ts:189) plus REVIEWER_CHAT_ID and REVIEWER_API.
    3. The prompt goes over stdin rather than argv, so nothing sensitive in a message lands in the process table.
  • Process
    $SHELL -l -c
    1. Turns run through a login, non-interactive shell (-l -c), so ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc are never sourced — the credential export has to be in ~/.zshenv/~/.zprofile or ~/.bash_profile.
    2. Every turn is a fresh shell, so a newly exported token is picked up without restarting the server — and equally, a token exported only in the server's own terminal session dies with it.
    3. The command -v guard means a missing CLI exits 127 with a plain message rather than looking like an auth failure.

    Model discovery runs its CLI probes through a login plus interactive shell (-l -i -c) while chat turns use -l -c, so a token exported from ~/.zshrc populates the model picker while every turn on that provider fails to authenticate.

  • Service
    result line → auth failure
    1. Auth failure is detected by matching a regex against the CLI's own reply text (claude-stream.ts:39), not by an exit code or an error field — a result line with is_error: false still settles as a failed turn.
    2. The login prompt is only scrubbed from the streamed reply when the buffer is under 200 characters (line 341), so a longer logged-out answer would be shown as the assistant's message and flagged as an error.
    3. Each provider owns its own pattern and hint: cursor's live in cursor-stream.ts:44 and 53, and codex/opencode have none at all.
  • Service
    finalizeTurn / loginHint
    1. This is the second detection site, for the case the parsers can't see: a CLI that dies with the login prompt on stderr and never emits a result line.
    2. It only inspects the last 500 characters of stderr (line 377), so a login prompt printed early in a noisy failure is missed and the raw tail is shown instead.
    3. loginHint returns null for codex and opencode (turn-parser.ts:81), so those two providers surface their raw CLI error with no remediation text.
  • Store
    completeTurn → chats.json

    The hint is written into chats.json as the turn's errorMessage, so a chat reopened after the developer has logged back in still shows the stale login advice on that old turn.

  • External
    The developer's own CLI login
    1. reviewer holds no LLM credential at all — there is no key field, no keychain entry, and no settings screen; the only occurrences of CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in the repo are inside the hint text on lines 72 and 81 of this file.
    2. Auth is therefore whatever the CLI already has on this machine: an interactive /login token, or a long-lived one from claude setup-token exported into the environment.
    3. Because the credential lives one process away, the server can only ever recognise a failure after the fact — it cannot pre-check whether a turn will authenticate.
    1. The remediation the hint suggests happens on a different rail: terminal threads launch the same CLIs through $SHELL -l -i inside a PTY, which is the only place an interactive /login can actually run.
    2. That PTY path is login and interactive, so it sources ~/.zshrc — which is exactly why a token exported there works when you type claude in a reviewer terminal but not in a chat turn.
